additional_info.subject: Note to ES
additional_info.body:
Suspected Root Cause : SECC not compatible with the VinFast 8
Problem Description : Vinfast try to test the intercompability with their new car VF8 with different charger manufecturer (see Vinfast analysis attached). Unfortunately, VF8 failed to charged with our Sicharge D.
Action Performed (L2) :  Analysis with VinFast.
Charger SW Version: 5.0.21 and 4.0.11
Reason for Handover (L3) : Need R&D involvement or VI
Fault history : N/A
Log analysis with timestamp :
We tested the chargers 1Vukib and jERN9L. Previously, they tried to charge on the Engie charger version 4.0.11 with similar findings.
Here are the results of the test:
First attempt on outlet 2 of 1Vukib at 12:36 GMT
: The session stopped in parameter discovery with an emergency shutdown from the EVSE. The error flag on the SIC D is 2024-11-25T12:36:51.123220+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/a7368e78fd94[714]: PLC-Error-Flag 'Outlet_DC2_codes' changed to true - (DC2 Errorcode:24). There is no SECC log generated for this session.
Second attempt on outlet 2 of 1Vukib at 12:37 GMT
: The session stopped in parameter discovery with an emergency shutdown from the EVSE. The error flag on the SIC D is 2024-11-25T12:36:51.123220+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/a7368e78fd94[714]: PLC-Error-Flag 'Outlet_DC2_codes' changed to true - (DC2 Errorcode:24). There is an SECC log generated. See attached. From the SECC, it's a SLAC failure.
Third attempt on outlet 1 of 1Vukib at 13:17 GMT
: The session was successful. SECC attached.
Fourth attempt on outlet 1 of 1Vukib at 13:56 GMT
: The session stopped in pre-charging. No error flag in the logs, but in the V2G logs, the CP signal unexpectedly went to B (suspect that the CP signal may be parasitic).
Fifth and sixth attempts on outlet 2 of 1Vukib
: The sessions stopped in parameter discovery with an emergency shutdown from the EVSE. The error flag on the SIC D is 2024-11-25T12:36:51.123220+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/a7368e78fd94[714]: PLC-Error-Flag 'Outlet_DC2_codes' changed to true - (DC2 Errorcode:24). There is an SECC log generated. See attached. From the SECC, it's a SLAC failure.
error code 24 is :
Outlet not ready - output voltage is too high to begin charging
Attachement
: SECC logs, Analysis from VinFast, Sicharge D Logs

Subject:
Sicharge D: Expert service support for ecar interop issues with Vinfast in Germany
Dear Jens.
We’ve received a ticket via ISP for some charging issues with the ecar Vinfast VF6. (link to ISP-ticket:
0392672
)
The manufacturer Vinfast has tested on their own and with NOC-support on a public Sicharge D in Germany (somewhere around Munich). There are only limited charger logs available from these sessions.
Vinfast has shared their findings with us and are asking for some support from our side to understand where their vehicle is behaving wrongly at the moment.
Our suggestion is to do the following steps:
Get in touch with Vinfast and organize a test session
Perform a test session and record charger logs
Analyze logs together with Vehicle OEM.
If applicable: open ticket to R&D.
We assume the efforts for ~8 hours.
We would allocate these hours with to the PLM budget for SichargeD-Expert services.
If you have any questions or objections please let us know.
Otherwise we would continue with the steps, starting on Wednesday.
Many thanks and best regards
Patrick

additional_info.body:
Dear Nghiêm Hoàng,
the support team reported the charging issues with Sicharge D and Vinfast vehicle. We checked the logs of the aborted charging session in Munich at 25.11.2024 and found various issues. Some session indicate a CP State change from C to B during cable check but other session show an interruption of the HighLevel Communication  during ChargeParameterDiscovery.
A detailed investigation of this problems requires a dircet alignment between charger and vehicle diagnosis. We could provide a test session in our Berlin Laboratory for an interoperability test between vehicle and Sicharge D. This test would allow us to trace some electrical parameter like CP-State or Isolatoin Supervision as well.
With best regards,
Ingo Oldenburg
eMobility Tech Support Team
https://siemens.sharepoint.com/teams/eMobilityServiceCollaboration
